facts.statement: The genus Mesembriornis was first described by the paleontologist Moreno in 1889.
Francisco Moreno described Mesembriornis in 1889 based on a cervical vertebra and leg bones found in Monte Hermoso, Argentina.
facts.quote: Mesembriornis was first described by Argentine paleontologist Francisco Moreno during the "Argentine Bone Wars" between him and Florentino Ameghino in 1889 based on a cervical vertebral centrum along with the proximal section of a right tibiotarsus and fibula

facts.statement: Mesembriornis lived on the pampas of eastern Argentina between 5.3 and 4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Mesembriornis lived on the pampa of eastern Argentina, from the Late Miocene to the Late Pliocene, roughly 5.3 to 4 million years ago.

facts.statement: Mesembriornis was one of the last terror birds to exist, living alongside the North American Titanis walleri.
facts.quote: Together with the North American giant Titanis walleri, it was among the last terror birds alive.

facts.statement: Mesembriornis was an intermediate-sized terror bird that could grow up to 1.5 meters tall.
facts.quote: Mesembriornis is a genus of intermediate-sized phorusrhacids that grew up to 1.5 m in height.

facts.statement: Mesembriornis was the lankiest of all terror birds, with its foot bone being 80 to 85% the length of its shin bone.
facts.quote: The genus is the lankiest of all the Phorusrhacids, where the Tarsometatarsus reaches a length of 80 to 85% of the length of the tibiotarsus.

facts.statement: Studies estimate Mesembriornis could run at 27 m/s, a speed comparable to a modern cheetah.
facts.quote: The paper found an estimate of 27 m/s, one of the highest speeds calculated for a terrestrial vertebrate, the speed being comparable to that of the modern spotted cheetah.

facts.statement: Scientists debate whether Mesembriornis's estimated high running speed was accurate or if its legs were primarily used for kicking prey.
facts.quote: However, the authors of the paper pointed out that the estimate could be inflated and that the use of the limbs was instead for kicking prey.

facts.statement: Under the kicking hypothesis, Mesembriornis could deliver kicks with 3.5 times its body weight, enough to break the bones of medium-sized mammals.
facts.quote: Following the "kicking" hypothesis, Mesembriornis was capable of delivering a kick with a force 3.5 times that of the body weight, a force capable of breaking the bones of modern medium-sized mammals like the springbok, Thomson's gazelle, and chamois.

facts.statement: Mesembriornis may have broken bones to access marrow, similar to how modern bearded vultures drop bones to break them.
facts.quote: This also means that Mesembriornis and other phorusrhacids could've accessed the bone marrow inside bones, a behavior done in the extant bearded vulture which has been observed breaking bones by dropping them from high altitudes.

facts.statement: Mesembriornis has had several synonyms including Hermosiornis, Palaeociconia australis, and Prophororhacos.
facts.quote: synonyms: * Hermosiornis Rovereto, 1914 Palaeociconia australis Moreno, 1889 Prophororhacos

facts.statement: Phylogenetic studies place Mesembriornis in a large clade that includes Procariama and Llallawavis.
facts.quote: which recovers Mesembriornis as a member of a large clade that includes Procariama and Llallawavis.

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database lists the time range for Mesembriornis as the Tortonian to Zanclean stages, from 8 to 3.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Tortonian to Zanclean (8 to 3.6 million years ago)
